raw_response:
It's October now, time to get the winter wheat in the ground. I've been back on the farm for 3 years — before that I worked construction in Shijiazhuang — so I'm still learning, but 340 mu is too much land to mess around with. My wife keeps the books and cooks for the hired hands, and our two kids are in school, so we need steady cash flow. I can't afford a bad year.

With 340 mu, I have to think like a business, but honestly I rely heavily on Old Wang from the east end of the village. He's been farming 25 years and knows every patch of soil. I also went to one extension training last spring about soil testing, but the lab is in Handan and costs too much, so I mostly go by look and feel, and what the extension guy said about general rates.

This year I'm putting 280 mu into wheat-maize double crop — that's my base, my insurance. The turnaround between wheat harvest and maize planting is brutal, sometimes only 5 or 6 days, so I rent a combine and a no-till planter. I bought a second-hand 90-horsepower tractor last year and I do the tillage and fertilizer spreading myself. The other 60 mu I'm splitting between peanut and soybean to spread my risk. Last year maize prices dropped right after harvest and I lost money waiting for them to come back. Peanut prices have been stable, and the extension agent says soybean is good for the soil, though I mostly care that it's cheap to plant.

**Cash is tight.** I need about 280,000–300,000 yuan for inputs this year. I have 70,000 in savings and I'll borrow the rest from the village credit cooperative. Every year this scares me. If wheat fails, I'm in real trouble.

For the **wheat** on 280 mu: I'll start planting around October 12th if it doesn't rain too hard. I'm buying improved Jinmai 47 seed — about 65 yuan per mu. I don't save seed at this scale; too risky. For fertilizer, I'll broadcast 50 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu before planting — that's 7.5 kg each of N, P, and K. Then at jointing in March, if the wheat looks green and healthy, I'll topdress 22 kg of urea per mu, giving another 10 kg N. So total N around 17.5 kg/mu. Last year I did 18 kg N and got 470 kg/mu. I'm hoping for 480–500 this year if spring cooperates. I'll irrigate 3 times — planting, wintering if dry, and jointing — at about 35 yuan/mu each time for electricity and labor. I also spray herbicide after emergence and a fungicide if I see rust.

For **maize** next summer on the same 280 mu: I'll plant hybrid Zhengdan 958 right after wheat harvest, around June 15th–18th. Seed is 55 yuan/mu. I'll put down 40 kg compound fertilizer at planting, then topdress urea at big trumpet stage. Total N around 16 kg/mu. I'll irrigate twice, maybe three times if July is dry. Target is 520 kg/mu. The hired guys know the drill now, but that window is always stressful.

For **peanut** on 30 mu: I'll plant in early May. Peanut needs less nitrogen but more calcium and potassium. I'll use 30 kg compound fertilizer plus some calcium powder as base. Irrigate twice. I expect about 280 kg/mu of pods. These 30 mu were fallow over winter — I ploughed them once in autumn to control weeds.

For **soybean** on 30 mu: I'll plant in late June, also on fallow land. Very cheap — just some phosphate fertilizer at planting and one irrigation if July is hot. Maybe 130 kg/mu. It's not big money, but if maize prices crash again, at least I have something else to sell.

I hired three local guys for the busy seasons and pay them 120 yuan per day. My wife and I handle supervision, record-keeping, and driving the tractor. We work from dawn to dark during planting and harvest. It's hard, but it's ours.
